title: Disclose shared-checkout overlap in published session records

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-418#disclose-shared-checkout-overlap

**Verdict: Caught.**

## What was checked

- **Story:** SEED-418#disclose-shared-checkout-overlap (`.planning/seeds/SEED-418-review-published-session-changes.md#disclose-shared-checkout-overlap`). Plan: `.planning/slice-plans/766-disclose-shared-checkout-overlap/PLAN.md`.
- **Revision:** ff3020f496b5734ca6734bf099c380a4c48157e3. Scratch worktree, detached, at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/22fb0da2/tmp/ic-scratch`. It was clean before the probe (`git status --porcelain` printed nothing).
- **Promise:** "Records and ranges without the mark stay readable and show no warning." In a published session whose second range is marked `uncertainty: "shared-checkout"`, the review of the unmarked first range does not carry `session.shared`. The review of the marked range does carry it.
- **Fault (the suggested one, used as given):** in `dashboard/server/publishedSessionReview.ts`, `publishedSessionReview` changed from
  `...(range.uncertainty === sharedCheckoutUncertainty && { shared: true }),`
  to
  `...(record.ranges.some((r) => r.uncertainty === sharedCheckoutUncertainty) && { shared: true }),`
  With this change the mark comes from any range in the record instead of the selected range.
- **Fixture:** the spec's own `aTwoRangeSession({ secondSharesCheckout: true })`. It builds two disjoint published pairs, puts another writer's revision between them, and marks only the second pair with `.sharingCheckout()`. The probe left it unchanged.
- **Maintained checks examined:**
  - `dashboard/backend-tests/review/published-session-ranges.spec.ts`
    - Line 105, "…when its unmarked first range is selected, then the review notes no shared checkout". This is the catching assertion: `expect(review).not.toHaveProperty("session.shared")` at line 111.
    - Line 93, the marked-range test.
  - `e2e/sessions/recently-done-published-sessions.spec.ts`, the shared-checkout test. I inspected it but did not run it. Its `closed()` helper publishes each session through a single `publishSessionClose` of one increment, so each record has one range. With one range, "any range marked" and "selected range marked" give the same result. That test cannot reach the faulted path, so it gives no verdict for this fault either way.

## Runs

Command for all three runs, in the scratch worktree: `env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run --silent test:dashboard:backend -- review/published-session-ranges`. Setup was Node v24.21.0, `/opt/homebrew/bin` first on PATH, and `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm` run first.

1. **Baseline:** 6 of 6 passed, both shared-checkout tests included (vitest reported 7.07s).
2. **Faulted:** 1 failed, 5 passed (5.69s).
   - Only line 105 failed: `AssertionError: expected { kind: 'published-session', …(6) } to not have property "session.shared"`, with Expected `undefined` and Received `true`.
   - **Reach:** the previous assertion in the same test, `toMatchObject({ selectedRun: "0" })`, passed. So the review really was the unmarked first range.
   - **Wrong behavior:** the received value shows the product returning `session.shared: true` for that range. That is the shared-checkout warning appearing on an unmarked range, which is the wrong behavior on the intended path.
   - The marked-range test at line 93 still passed, as it should, since the fault does not change the marked range.
3. **Restored:** a shell `trap … EXIT` undid the edit with `git checkout -- dashboard/server/publishedSessionReview.ts`. Afterwards `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` printed nothing, so the scratch worktree matched its pre-probe state; the gitignored `node_modules` and vitest `test-results` were not shown. The rerun passed 6 of 6 (5.80s).

**Cleanup:** removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove --force`. `--force` was needed only because of the gitignored install and test-result files. `git worktree list` no longer shows it. I did not edit, stash or reset the execution checkout. It currently shows ` M .planning/PRODUCT-BACKLOG.md`, which this probe did not cause and left alone.

## Next proof action

None for this promise. The backend range spec catches the fault on the multi-range path. No new repair decision comes from this probe.

Two related notes:
- This catch is the `not.toHaveProperty("session.shared")` assertion that the story moved from `published-session-review.spec.ts` into the range spec. So the relocated assertion still guards the promise.
- The e2e shared-checkout journey covers only single-range records. Whether a browser journey should also cover the mixed-range case is for the caller to decide. This probe does not show that the backend catch leaves a gap.

## Cost

- **Test runtime (measured, vitest-reported duration):** about 18.6 s in total over 3 runs (7.07 s + 5.69 s + 5.80 s). This leaves out `npm` dependency installation in the fresh worktree, which took roughly 1–2 minutes of wall time (estimated, not timed).
- **Human effort:** unavailable. No human took part during the probe, and there is no separate measure.
- **Agent effort:** unavailable as a measured figure; the agent has no token or turn counter. Estimated at about 12 tool calls by one agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 85599 ms (measured), from 1795331713911 to 1795331799510 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

ff3020f496b5734ca6734bf099c380a4c48157e3 — Caught; no follow-up.
